lead: A diode bridge with a large capacitor draws current in short spikes near the mains peak. The current is not sine-shaped, so the rectifier has a poor power factor even when the current is almost in phase with the voltage. A power factor correction (PFC) rectifier adds a switching stage that forces the input current to follow the sine voltage, so the supply sees a resistor. Laptop and desktop supplies, LED drivers above roughly 25 W, and EV chargers and fast chargers above roughly 75 W use PFC to meet harmonic limits and to use the grid better.
prereq: You need: power factor, displacement factor and THD from 2.5, and the boost converter idea from Unit 3.

sections.h3: Why a capacitor-input rectifier has poor power factor

blocks.text: A diode bridge with a capacitor is the cheapest DC source. The capacitor charges to the mains peak. Diodes conduct only while the instantaneous mains voltage is above the capacitor voltage. Current flows in narrow pulses at the peak, not over the whole cycle. The RMS current is high for the power delivered, and the pulses contain large harmonics.

Power factor is real power divided by apparent power: PF = P/(V<sub>rms</sub> I<sub>rms</sub>). P is average power in W, V<sub>rms</sub> and I<sub>rms</sub> are RMS voltage and current. For a sine voltage, PF = displacement factor × distortion factor. Displacement factor is cos φ<sub>1</sub>, where φ<sub>1</sub> is the phase of the current fundamental. Distortion factor is I<sub>1,rms</sub>/I<sub>rms</sub>, where I<sub>1,rms</sub> is fundamental RMS current.

The current pulses sit at the voltage peak, so φ<sub>1</sub> is near zero and displacement factor is near one. Distortion factor is low. Total harmonic distortion (THD) is the RMS harmonic current divided by the fundamental. High THD gives low distortion factor and poor PF. The capacitor does not correct PF; it makes the current peakier.

Passive PFC adds a series inductor. The inductor slows current rise and spreads each pulse over a wider angle. THD falls moderately and PF improves. The inductor carries 50 Hz current, so it is large, heavy and costly. It cannot meet tight harmonic limits at high power.

sections.h3: Active boost PFC: current follows the voltage

blocks.text: An active PFC rectifier places a boost cell after the diode bridge. The bridge gives a rectified sine, |v<sub>in</sub>|. The boost cell has inductor L, switch S and diode D. When S is on, L stores energy. When S is off, L current flows through D to the 400 V bus. The switch works at high frequency, far above 50 Hz.

The inner current loop measures inductor current and compares it with a reference. The reference comes from a multiplier. One input is a scaled copy of |v<sub>in</sub>|. The other is the output of a slow error amplifier comparing the bus voltage with 400 V. The result is i<sub>ref</sub> = k |v<sub>in</sub>|, where k is set by the voltage loop. The current loop switches S so average input current equals i<sub>ref</sub>. Thus i<sub>in</sub> is proportional to v<sub>in</sub>, and the mains sees an effective resistance R<sub>e</sub> = V<sub>rms</sub><sup>2</sup>/P, where R<sub>e</sub> is the effective input resistance in Ω, V<sub>rms</sub> is the RMS mains voltage in V and P is the input real power in W.

The boost duty is D = 1 − v<sub>in</sub>/V<sub>dc</sub>, where v<sub>in</sub> is instantaneous rectified voltage and V<sub>dc</sub> is bus voltage. At the 230 V mains peak, v<sub>in</sub> = 325.3 V. With V<sub>dc</sub> = 400 V, D = 0.19. Near zero crossings D rises towards 1. A boost converter only raises voltage, so the bus must be above the mains peak; 400 V gives margin.

The voltage loop must be slow. Single-phase power pulsates at twice mains frequency, so the bus has 100 Hz ripple. A fast loop would put that ripple into the current reference and distort the input current. Loop bandwidth is kept below 100 Hz, often 10–20 Hz. Continuous conduction mode (CCM) is used at higher power; discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) appears at light load. Both can give PF near 0.99 and THD below 5%.

A bridgeless PFC removes the diode bridge. Current uses two switches, saving one diode drop and raising efficiency. Current sensing and EMI are harder because the mains is not tied to the bus. An interleaved PFC runs two boost cells 180° apart. Input ripple partly cancels, inductors shrink, and heat spreads. Server supplies and EV chargers use these versions.

The 400 V bus is not a battery. The bus capacitor is sized for 100 Hz ripple and hold-up time, not long storage. The PFC stage sets input current shape; a second DC-DC converter usually gives isolation and a regulated low voltage. Harmonic standards limit grid current. IEC 61000-3-2 covers many low-power types of equipment (rated input current up to 16 A per phase); IEEE 519 covers industrial installations. PFC is not efficiency: a supply can have PF 0.99 and still waste heat. At light load, some controllers enter burst mode to keep efficiency high.

examples.question: A 500 W PFC rectifier runs from a 230 V, 50 Hz mains with power factor 0.99 and a 400 V output bus. Assume ideal devices and sinusoidal input current. Find the input RMS current, the peak input current, the peak mains voltage, and the boost switch duty at the mains peak.
steps: Real power P = 500 W. PF = P/(V<sub>rms</sub> I<sub>rms</sub>), so I<sub>rms</sub> = P/(PF × V<sub>rms</sub>) = 500/(0.99 × 230) = 2.196 A ≈ 2.2 A.
For a sine current, peak current I<sub>pk</sub> = √2 × I<sub>rms</sub> = √2 × 2.196 = 3.105 A ≈ 3.1 A.
Peak mains voltage V<sub>pk</sub> = √2 × 230 = 325.269 V ≈ 325.3 V.
Boost duty at the peak: D = 1 − V<sub>pk</sub>/V<sub>dc</sub> = 1 − 325.269/400 = 0.1868 ≈ 0.19. Duty rises towards 1 as v<sub>in</sub> falls towards zero.
examples.answer: The input RMS current is 2.2 A, the peak input current is 3.1 A, the peak mains voltage is 325.3 V, and the duty at the mains peak is 0.19.
examples.check:
import math
P = 500.0
pf = 0.99
Vrms = 230.0
Vdc = 400.0
Irms = P / (pf * Vrms)
Ipk = math.sqrt(2) * Irms
Vpk = math.sqrt(2) * Vrms
D = 1 - Vpk / Vdc
print(round(Irms, 1))
print(round(Ipk, 1))
print(round(Vpk, 1))
print(round(D, 2))

traps: A capacitor filter improves power factor. It does the opposite: it narrows diode conduction and raises THD.
PF = cos φ is enough for any rectifier. It is true only for sine current; with harmonics PF = displacement factor × distortion factor.
PFC and efficiency are the same. PF = P/S; efficiency = Pout/Pin. A supply can have PF 0.99 and low efficiency.
The PFC voltage loop should be fast to hold 400 V. A fast loop copies 100 Hz bus ripple into the current reference and distorts input current.
A 400 V bus is arbitrary. The boost can only step up, so the bus must exceed the 325.3 V peak of a 230 V mains.

quiz.q: Define THD for an input current with fundamental RMS I<sub>1</sub> and total RMS I.
quiz.a: THD = √(I² − I<sub>1</sub>²)/I<sub>1</sub>, the RMS harmonic current divided by the fundamental.

quiz.q: Why does a capacitor-input rectifier have near-unity displacement factor but poor power factor?
quiz.a: Its current pulses are at the voltage peak, so φ<sub>1</sub> ≈ 0. The pulse shape has large harmonics, so distortion factor is low and THD is high.

quiz.q: A 200 W load runs from 230 V with PF 0.95. Find the input RMS current.
A boost PFC has a 400 V bus. Find the duty when v<sub>in</sub> = 200 V.
Why is the PFC voltage loop kept slow?
quiz.a: The bus has 100 Hz ripple from single-phase power. A slow loop keeps that ripple out of the current reference, so the input current stays sine-shaped.

quiz.q: Why must the bus be above 325.3 V for a 230 V mains?
quiz.a: The boost cell only steps up. If the bus voltage were below the mains peak (325.3 V), then near the top of each half-cycle the rectified input would exceed the bus, the bridge diodes would conduct straight into the bus, and the switch would lose control of the inductor current. 400 V keeps the bus above the peak with margin.

beyond: Not for the exam. Totem-pole PFC removes the bridge and uses fast legs; SiC or GaN switches make it practical at high power. Digital control can shape current, handle protection and communicate. Bridgeless and interleaved PFC are common in server and EV chargers. Search for totem-pole PFC, average current mode control and IEC 61000-3-2.
